description.narrative:
National Democratic Institute (NDI) har ansökt om finansiering på 13 601 800 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Advancing Gender Equality through Women’s Political Participation" i Nordmakedonien under perioden 2020-2023.
Projektets syfte är att minska de institutionella, sociokulturella och individuella hindren för kvinnors egenmakt och därigenom öka kvinnors meningsfulla politiska deltagande samt främja jämställdhet på lokal nivå och inom de politiska partierna.
Insatsen ämnar att - förbättra jämställdheten inom politiska partier genom att bidra till att övervinna interna hinder som hämmar kvinnors politiska deltagande och ledarskap. Detta inkluderar aktiviteter för att öka medvetenheten om vikten av och fördelarna med att integrera jämställdhet inom partistrukturerna. Att bygga kapacitet hos politiskt aspirerande unga kvinnor och män att ta ledarpositioner inom politiska partier är ett mervärde som väntas intensifiera ovanstående process.
- ge kvinnliga kandidater kompetens att framgångsrikt bedriva kampanjer under lokalvalet 2021 och att styra på lokal nivå. Utbildning inom förvaltningsarbete ska tillhandahållas för de framröstade kvinnliga politikerna för att förse dem med färdigheter för att kunna utföra sina roller.
- minska 'våldet mot kvinnor i politiken' (VAW-P) genom att använda information från forskning som visar omfattningen och djupet av VAW-P. Informationen ska ge vägledning till kommuner som antar jämställdhetsfunktioner och jämställdhetskommittéer för att skapa trygga miljöer för kvinnor att utöva ledarskap och beslutsfattande makt. Allmänhetens medvetenhet och utbildning om VAW-P kommer belysas genom kampanjen "It´s Not OK".
Insatsens projektlängd är 32 månader och den begärda budgeten uppgår till 13 601 800 SEK.

The National Democratic Institute has applied to Sida for funding of 13 601 800 SEK to carry out the "Advancing Gender Equality through Women’s Political Participation" in North Macedonia during the period 2020-2023.
The project aim is to reduce the institutional, socio-cultural and individual barriers to women's empowerment, and thereby to increase women's meaningful political participation and to advance gender equality at local governance level and within the political parties.
The proposed concept is set to: - Improve gender equality in political parties, by supporting in overcoming the internal barriers that impede women's political participation and leadership. Raising awareness on the importance and the benefits in streamlining the gender equality within the political party structures would be attended through cross-section work with the political parties. Building capacity for politically aspirant young women and men to take leadership positions within political parties is an added value that would intensify the above process. - Provide women candidates with the skills to campaign successfully during the local elections in 2021 and to govern at the local level. Good governance practices training shall be provided for the elected women officials in order to equip them with skills to ably carry out their roles. - Reduce violence against women in politics (VAW-P), by utilizing the information of the research undertaken under USAID funding on the scope and depth of VAW-P to provide guidance to municipalities that enact gender focal points and equal opportunity committees to create safe local governance environments for women to exercise leadership and decision-making power. Public awareness raising and education on VAW-P shall be attended through implementing the "It's Not OK" campaign.
The suggested program duration is 32 months and the requested budget is 13 601 800 SEK.

The project's overall goal is to lower the individual, socio-cultural, and institutional barriers to women's political participation through a series of interrelated interventions. The project objectives are to: - Improve gender equality in political parties by working with a cross-section of political parties to raise their awareness of the importance and benefits of streamlining gender equality within political party structures - Provide women candidates with the skills and a supportive environment to campaign successfully for and govern at the local level and in the Parliament , by providing technical assistance to women candidates for municipal councils, mayoral positions and Members of Parliament, and training the elected women officials in good governance practices in order to equip them with the skills to ably carry out their roles - Reduce violence against women in politics (VAW-P), by supporting the municipal authorities with guidance to create safe local governance environments for women to exercise leadership and decision-making power. Raising public awareness of VAW-P will be implemented with a national educational campaign "It's Not OK". The project is developed based on 20 years experience of NDI and their work in the country. The project responds to the Results strategy for Swedens reform cooperation with Eastern Europe, the Western Balkans and Turkey 2014 2020, and it is backing the task of Swedish support to help ensure that gender equality issues are given greater political priority and that initiatives strengthen womens and girls empowerment and opportunities to enjoy their rights. It contributes by "altering about gender-stereotyped attitudes and unequal gender roles". Moreover, strengthening political participation of women is among the 13 priorities in the governments initiative Drive for democracy, and an objective of the Swedens feminist foreign policy. The political parties, local authorities and individual women candidates for leadership positions in politics as well as the general public are to be affected by this project, and they will be influenced to change their attitude, to become more gender aware and supportive to gender equality in politics.

description.narrative:
Since the project initiation date, the project has shown a very good progress. Among other the project contributed that eight political parties from the country including all of the biggest political parties, agreed to actively take part in implementation of the project and to provide representatives in the project established Gender Equality Task Force (GETF). The GETF is established in order to assess gender equality practices within political parties. The project operations have lead toward raised awareness on the need to strengthen women participation in politics in the country. The political parties are recognizing this need and have reacted by introducing changes in their functioning in their respective parties with activities like: - GETF members formed the Movement Besa Women Forum; - DUI and Alternativa created a separate leadership academy; - A Training of Trainers started the ninth generation of SDSMs School for Women Activism; - Gender-sensitive language is introduced into the LDP statute; - A discussion of a pilot leadership and mentorship program is initiated by VMRO-DPMNE. - A total number of 76 individuals are trained on election campaign skills, out of which: 2 ran as mayoral candidates, 31 ran on the electoral lists for municipal council (18 reported to be elected out of which 2 elected for presidents of municipal councils in municipality Ilinden and Sveti Nikole), 23 were otherwise involved in senior leadership roles on electoral campaigns, including campaign management, communications, and volunteer management, and 3 did not end up playing a role in election campaigns. - Capacity building and knowledge increase have been implemented for local government officials distributed in 21 different municipalities throughout the territory of the country and representing 12 political parties, including all of the major political parties in the country. - 22 municipalities signed Commitment for advancing gender equality and elimination of violence against women in politics, and share experiences in recognizing the needs and approaches how to advance gender equality on the local level and to reduce VAW-P.
Besides the political parties, youth - members of the Youth Leadership Academy are a target group that will present policy papers on topics including sport, digitization, and culture. The project activities in this field resulted with:
- Organized initiative Young People Take Over, where eleven active participants of the Youth Leadership Academy (eight women and three men) were provided with the opportunity to shadow elected officials and to gain insight into the roles of public officials including: the speaker of the parliament, secretary general of parliament, chairs of parliamentary committees and others. The initiative was supported by the Minister of Labor and Social Policy, and it was encouraged for further engagement, so young people could feel inspired to be more involved in the political decision-making process.
- Organized training through the Youth Leadership Academy . The fourth training was organized under the title "My Point of View" , which was manly addressing building capacity in rapport-building, consensus - building and engaging in political debates and dialogue.
The cooperation with the Civil Society sector resulted with established cooperation with a local CSO - Reactor, that conducted a research evaluating the socioeconomic conditions influencing women's political participation in North Macedonia.
Moreover, the parliamentary Council for Equal Opportunity exchanged information to learn best practices and key shortcomings in the implementation of legislation related to Violence Against Women in Politics, hate speech, harassment at the workplace, and any aspects related to gender equality. - Engagement with male politicians and electoral candidates has commenced, and an increase in knowledge on masculinity issues and awareness of VAW-P is reported. A workshop with a group of 36 men on increasing awareness for gender equality and gender-sensitive institutional practices is organized. - Widespread media campaign was organized against Violence against women in politics and hate speech. The campaign included use of billboards including a Wall of Shame positioned in the Center of Skopje which highlighted and condemned real examples of hate speech used during the local election campaign - www.nezanasilstvo.mk. - A Code of Conduct for Fair and Democratic Elections was developed by the State Election Commission and NDI, condemning gendered hate speech and discrimination. The Code of Conduct was signed by 17 political parties (SDSM, VMRO-DPMNE, Besa, Alternativa, DUI, Alliance for Albanians, LDP, DOM, GROM, DPA, Integra, Levica, PODEM, Democratic Party of the Turks in Macedonia, Party of the Movement of Turks in Macedonia, Bosnian Democratic Alliance, Green Humane City), as well as by 10,831 individual candidates including the entire pool of election candidates (approx. 4,763 women).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
